subject: Clarifying BAA eligibility and PHI handling for St. Augustine Health
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@staugustinehealth.org>
To: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Jorge Rivera <jorge.rivera@staugustinehealth.org>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: BAA question — are we eligible to send PHI to Redwood hosted API?

Hi Dev,

Quick question as we're scoping an integration: our team wants to run short clinical note summaries through Redwood to extract structured fields. The pipeline will include patient identifiers in prompts (MRN, DOB) during the POC. Before we proceed we need to confirm whether Redwood will sign a BAA for the hosted API, and if not, what configuration (Dedicated, Private) is required to process PHI.

Specifics: approximate volume is small for POC (estimated ~50k tokens/day), and we need to ensure prompts are not persisted, that KV/prefix caches can be disabled, and that logs containing prompts can be restricted. Can you clarify the options and any required controls?

Thanks,
Maria Lopez
Security & Compliance Program Manager
St. Augustine Health

Attachments: none

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@staugustinehealth.org>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BAA question — are we eligible to send PHI to Redwood hosted API?

Hi Maria — thanks for the clear summary. Short answer: we can support PHI but the recommended deployment depends on your risk and contractual requirements. A few quick points and follow-ups so we can provide a definitive answer: 

- Hosted API (multi-tenant): by default, we process requests transiently and do not persist customer prompts for model training. However, we have stricter criteria for signing BAAs on the hosted tier (audit, account isolation, and specific logging controls).
- Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity): provides tenant isolation on dedicated GPU pools; options to disable KV/prefix caching per-route and configure log retention. Often a good middle ground for customers who need predictable throughput but not full on-prem control.
- Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem): highest assurance — customer-managed network, optional HSM/KMS integrations, and full control over data persistence and audit logs.

Questions for your team: will you require customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)? Do you need audit log retention beyond standard SLA? Any regulators or auditors we should expect to engage with?

I'll attach our SOC 2 summary and a standard BAA template for your security team to review. If it's helpful I can loop in our Security Engineers and Solutions Architect for a short call to walk the architecture and DPIA items. Proposed next step: 30-minute call tomorrow or early next week.

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev.patel@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments referenced: redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf; redwood_baa_template.docx

Subject: Re: BAA question — are we eligible to send PHI to Redwood hosted API?

Thanks Dev — a couple clarifications from our side: 

- Yes, identifiers will be present in prompts during POC. We plan to scrub or hash MRNs before production, but POC will have plaintext identifiers.
- Traffic is low for the POC (~50k tokens/day) but could grow quickly.
- Our compliance team insists that any caching that could result in persistent KV entries with PHI must be disabled.
- We need to know whether alerts/logs will capture prompt text (and if so whether we can restrict/obfuscate them).

If you can confirm those items and share the BAA template + SOC2, we can start our internal review. Also please share an architecture diagram that shows flow of data and where logs are generated/stored.

Regards,
Jorge Rivera
Integration Engineering Lead
St. Augustine Health

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Rivera <jorge.rivera@staugustinehealth.org>, Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@staugustinehealth.org>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BAA question — are we eligible to send PHI to Redwood hosted API?

Hi Jorge / Maria — thanks for the specifics. Below are concrete answers and recommended next steps: 

1) Prompt persistence: our default hosted offering does not persist prompts for training. Prompts are processed transiently and cleared from the inference layer after generation. We do collect operational logs (request IDs, latency, routing) but request and response payloads are not retained in long-term analytics by default. For customers requiring zero retention of prompt text in logs we offer a "no-payload-logging" configuration that scrubs payloads at the edge.

2) KV/prefix cache: this is configurable per-route. For any route handling PHI we can disable KV caching to ensure no model-side cache retains identifiers.

3) Logs and alerting: by default some diagnostic traces may include hashed request IDs. We can provide a hardened logging profile where payloads are never logged and traces reference only request IDs. For Dedicated/Private customers you can opt into sending logs to your own secure logging endpoint (SIEM) or S3 bucket.

4) BAA signing policy: Redwood will sign BAAs for Hosted customers who meet certain account-level controls (contract, annual SOC2 review, and an agreed no-payload-logging config). For heightened assurance or where auditors require customer-managed keys, we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with KMS integration.

Attachments included for your review: redwood_SOC2_report_2026.pdf (summary of controls), redwood_baa_template.docx, phi_processing_matrix.csv (shows default vs configurable behaviors for storage, caching, and logging).

Next steps I propose:
- Share these artifacts with your compliance & infra teams (attached).
- Quick 30-minute technical call with our Security Engineer (Evelyn) and Solutions Architect to review the architecture diagram and DPIA checklist.
- If terms align, we can issue a DocuSign BAA and mark the account with the no-payload-logging flag ahead of the POC.

Proposed times: Tue 2026-07-14 09:00-12:00 PT or Wed 2026-07-15 13:00-16:00 PT. Which works for your CISO?

Best,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
